subject: water strider
title: The Water Strider Doesn't Walk on Water. It Rows Like a Boat

scenes.text: The insect that walks on water isn't walking at all.
Its legs are covered in fine hairs that keep them from getting wet, and they press tiny dimples into the surface.
But it moves by sculling its middle legs like oars, and the surface springs back like a trampoline.
Scientists at M.I.T. found that the push comes from swirls under the surface, not from waves.
Even newborn striders can row this way. It's rowing, not walking, and the pond is the boat.
